tools.name: show_api_key
tools.description: Return the bearer token from MCP settings. For debugging.

tools.name: primer
tools.description: Current time, user location and network environment for the session. Use before answering anything time- or location-dependent.

tools.name: guess_datetime_url
tools.description: Guess when a page was published or last updated, with a confidence score. Checks HTTP headers, metadata, Schema.org, visible dates, feeds and sitemaps.

tools.name: capture_screenshot_url
tools.description: Screenshot a page as base64 JPEG. Use when the page must be seen rather than read.

firstScreenOnly.description: Capture only the first screen instead of the full page. Faster.

return_url.description: Return URLs instead of base64 images.

tools.name: read_url
tools.description: Fetch a URL (page or PDF) as clean markdown. Pass `question` to get only the passages answering it instead of the whole page - far cheaper than reading the full body into context.

url.description: Page or PDF URL, or up to 5 URLs to read in parallel.

withAllLinks.description: Also return every link on the page.

withAllImages.description: Also return every image on the page.

question.description: Return only the passages answering this question, instead of the full body. Omit for the whole page.

chunk_size.description: Passage size in words, default 100. Larger gives more surrounding context, smaller pinpoints the answer. Comparable across scripts. Needs `question`.

tools.name: search_web
tools.description: Search the web. Returns titles, URLs and search-engine snippets.

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: search_web_deep
tools.description: Search the web, then read each result page and return the passage that best answers the query. Use when the answer is in page text rather than in titles or snippets. Slower than search_web (2-20s).

num.description: Results to return, 1-10. Each is a fully-read page, so higher is slower.

snippet_source.description: 'auto' keeps whichever is better, the page passage or the engine snippet. 'content' returns only page passages and omits unreadable pages, so you may get fewer than num.

tools.name: expand_query
tools.description: Rewrite one query into several diverse queries, for broader search coverage.

tools.name: search_arxiv
tools.description: Search arXiv preprints (physics, maths, CS, quantitative biology and finance).

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: search_ssrn
tools.description: Search SSRN working papers (social science, economics, law, finance, management).

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: search_jina_blog
tools.description: Search Jina AI's news and blog at jina.ai/news: product announcements, model releases, technical write-ups.

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: search_images
tools.description: Search the web for images. Returns base64 JPEGs by default.

return_url.description: Return URLs and metadata instead of base64 images.

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: parallel_search_web
tools.description: Run several web searches at once. Give queries covering different angles of the topic; expand_query can generate them.

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: parallel_search_arxiv
tools.description: Run several arXiv searches at once. Give queries covering different research angles.

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: parallel_search_ssrn
tools.description: Run several SSRN searches at once. Give queries covering different research angles.

tbs.description: Age limit: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m, qdr:y (hour to year).

tools.name: parallel_read_url
tools.description: Read several URLs at once.

withAllLinks.description: Also return every link on the page.

withAllImages.description: Also return every image on the page.

question.description: Return only the passages answering this question, instead of the full body.

chunk_size.description: Passage size in words, default 100. Needs `question`.

tools.name: classify_text
tools.description: Classify texts into labels you supply, using Jina embeddings. Zero-shot: no training data needed.

tools.name: sort_by_relevance
tools.description: Rerank documents by relevance to a query, using Jina Reranker.

tools.name: deduplicate_strings
tools.description: Select the top-k semantically distinct strings from a list, dropping near-duplicates.

k.description: How many to keep. Omit to pick k automatically from diminishing returns.

tools.name: deduplicate_images
tools.description: Select the top-k visually distinct images (URLs or base64) from a list, dropping near-duplicates.

images.description: Images to deduplicate, up to 200. Each is an http(s) URL or raw base64.

k.description: How many to keep. Omit to pick k automatically from diminishing returns.

tools.name: search_bibtex
tools.description: Find papers and return ready-to-use BibTeX entries. Searches DBLP and Semantic Scholar.

tools.name: extract_pdf
tools.description: Extract figures, tables and equations from a PDF as images, by arXiv id or URL.

id.description: arXiv id, e.g. '2301.12345'. Give id or url.

url.description: PDF URL. Give id or url.

max_edge.description: Longest image edge in pixels, default 1024.

type.description: Comma-separated types to keep: figure, table, equation. Default all.

jina-mcp-server.instructions:
Web access: search the live web, read URLs, search academic papers, and run Jina embedding/reranker utilities.

Use for anything online - current events, a URL the user pasted, a claim needing a source. Not for local files, code execution, or databases.

Picking a tool:
- search_web returns engine snippets. search_web_deep reads each result page and returns the passage that answers the query - slower, use when the answer is inside a page rather than in its title.
- read_url fetches one page as markdown. Pass its `question` to get only the answering passages instead of the whole body; this is much cheaper than reading a full page into context.
- Prefer the parallel_* variants over repeated single calls.
- search_arxiv for preprints, search_ssrn for social science and finance, search_bibtex for citations, search_jina_blog for Jina's own models and releases.
- primer supplies the current time and user location; call it before answering anything time- or location-dependent.

tools.name: web_search_exa
tools.description:
Search the web for any topic and get clean, ready-to-use content.

      Best for: Finding current information, news, facts, people, companies, or answering questions about any topic.
      Returns: Clean text content from top search results.

      Query tips:
      describe the ideal page, not keywords. "blog post comparing React and Vue performance" not "React vs Vue".
      Use category:people / category:company to search through Linkedin profiles / companies respectively.
      If highlights are insufficient, follow up with web_fetch_exa on the best URLs.

query.description: Natural language search query. Should be a semantically rich description of the ideal page, not just keywords. Optionally include category:<type> (company, people) to focus results — e.g. 'category:people John Doe software engineer'.

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 10).

tools.name: web_fetch_exa
tools.description:
Read a webpage's full content as clean markdown. Use after web_search_exa when highlights are insufficient or to read any URL.

Best for: Extracting full content from known URLs. Batch multiple URLs in one call.
Returns: Clean text content and metadata from the page(s).

urls.description: URLs to read. Batch multiple URLs in one call.

maxCharacters.description: Maximum characters to extract per page (default: 3000)

resources.name: tools_list
resources.description: List of available Exa tools and their descriptions

tools.name: activate_window
tools.description: Focus a Linux desktop window by window_id, pid, app_id, wm_class, title, or terminal selectors when the compositor permits it.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element by index, semantic selector, or desktop coordinate pixels from screenshot metadata.

relative.description:
Interpret `x`/`y` as relative to the targeted window's top-left corner
(the same coordinate space as a window-cropped `screenshot`). Requires a
window target; ignored otherwise.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Report Linux Computer Use desktop integration readiness.

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag from one point to another using pixel coordinates.

tools.name: focused_window
tools.description: Return the compositor window that currently has keyboard focus.

tools.name: get_app_state
tools.description: Start an app use session if needed, then get a size-bounded screenshot and accessibility state for a Linux app. Screenshot results include coordinate_width, coordinate_height, scale, format, and quality when the returned image is downscaled or compressed; callers can request jpeg/quality for compression before resizing.

format.description: Output image format (default png). Use jpeg with quality to trade exact pixels for smaller payloads.

max_bytes.description: Maximum returned screenshot image bytes before base64 (default 2 MiB, hard-capped).

max_depth.description: Maximum AT-SPI traversal depth (default 32, hard max 64).

max_height.description: Maximum returned screenshot height in pixels (default 1920, hard-capped).

max_nodes.description: Maximum raw AT-SPI nodes to inspect before compaction (default 1000, hard max 2000).

max_width.description: Maximum returned screenshot width in pixels (default 1920, hard-capped).

quality.description: JPEG quality from 1 to 95 (default 80). Ignored for png.

scale.description: Additional downscale factor from 0.0 to 1.0, applied before max dimensions.

verbose.description:
Include the full diagnostics report (large). Default false: only the
compact readiness block is returned.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List running Linux desktop app candidates visible to the Computer Use backend.

tools.name: list_windows
tools.description: List compositor windows with title, app id, class, focus state, client type, and known bounds.

tools.name: move_window
tools.description: Move a window to a new desktop position (frame top-left in desktop coordinates). Useful to recover windows that are partially off-screen. Works through the computer-use-linux GNOME Shell extension or a generic X11/EWMH window manager (wmctrl).

tools.name: perform_action
tools.description: Invoke an accessibility action exposed by an element selected by index, identifier, or semantic selector. Defaults to the primary action unless action is provided.

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Press a key or key-combination on the keyboard, optionally after focusing a target window or terminal selector. Key grammar (case-insensitive; hyphens/spaces ignored): combos join with '+', e.g. Ctrl+L or Ctrl+Shift+T. Modifiers: ctrl/control, alt/option, shift, meta/super/cmd/command. Named keys: enter/return, escape/esc, tab, backspace, delete/del, space, home, end, pageup, pagedown, arrowleft/left, arrowright/right, arrowup/up, arrowdown/down, f1-f12. Plus single US letters a-z and digits 0-9. Anything else returns an error (never silently dropped). On Wayland, chords are sent through an active remote desktop portal keyboard session when one is available (or when ydotool is absent), falling back to ydotool otherwise. Note: compositor-level shortcuts (e.g. Super+Up) may be consumed by GNOME before reaching the app.

tools.name: resize_window
tools.description: Resize a window to a new frame width/height in desktop pixels, unmaximizing it first if needed. Useful to fit a window fully on-screen. Works through the computer-use-linux GNOME Shell extension or a generic X11/EWMH window manager (wmctrl).

height.description: New frame height in desktop pixels.

width.description: New frame width in desktop pixels.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the screen and return it as a viewable, size-bounded image. Optionally target a window (window_id/pid/wm_class/title/app_id): the window is raised to the front and the image is cropped before any resize. Returns the image plus a short caption with returned dimensions, coordinate dimensions, scale, format, quality, source, and crop bounds; callers can request jpeg/quality for compression before resizing.

format.description: Output image format (default png). Use jpeg with quality to trade exact pixels for smaller payloads.

full_screen.description: Capture the whole desktop even when a window is targeted (default false).

max_bytes.description: Maximum returned screenshot image bytes before base64 (default 2 MiB, hard-capped).

max_height.description: Maximum returned screenshot height in pixels (default 1920, hard-capped).

max_width.description: Maximum returned screenshot width in pixels (default 1920, hard-capped).

quality.description: JPEG quality from 1 to 95 (default 80). Ignored for png.

raise_window.description:
Raise the targeted window before capture (default true). Ignored without
a window target.

scale.description: Additional downscale factor from 0.0 to 1.0, applied before max dimensions.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll an element in a direction by a number of pages. With a window target and no x/y/element_index, scrolls at the centre of the targeted window.

relative.description:
Interpret `x`/`y` as relative to the targeted window's top-left corner
(the same coordinate space as a window-cropped `screenshot`). Requires a
window target; ignored otherwise.

tools.name: set_value
tools.description: Set the value of a settable accessibility element selected by index, identifier, or semantic selector.

tools.name: setup_accessibility
tools.description: Enable GNOME accessibility through gsettings so Linux Computer Use can read AT-SPI trees.

tools.name: setup_window_targeting
tools.description: Install and enable the optional GNOME Shell extension used for exact window list/focus targeting when GNOME blocks native introspection.

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type literal text using keyboard input, optionally after focusing a target window or terminal selector.

computer-use-linux.instructions: Begin every turn that uses Computer Use by calling get_app_state. If diagnostics report disabled GNOME accessibility, call setup_accessibility before asking the user to retry. Use list_windows/focused_window before targeted keyboard input. If diagnostics report windowing.can_list_windows=false on GNOME, call setup_window_targeting to install the optional GNOME Shell extension backend, then ask the user to log out and back in if the setup report says a shell reload is required. This Linux backend can capture size-bounded screenshots through GNOME Shell or XDG Desktop Portal, read AT-SPI trees with action/value metadata, invoke native AT-SPI actions, set AT-SPI values or editable text, list/focus compositor windows through registered Linux window backends when the session permits it, attach best-effort terminal tty/process metadata to terminal windows, send coordinate or element-targeted click/scroll/drag input through the Wayland remote desktop portal when available, and send layout-safe literal type_text through KDE clipboard integration on Plasma Wayland or through portal keysyms on other Wayland sessions before falling back to ydotool. Screenshot results include width/height for the returned image plus coordinate_width/coordinate_height and scale for desktop coordinate conversion; request more detail with max_width, max_height, max_bytes, format=jpeg, quality, or a smaller target/crop instead of relying on unbounded screenshots. Tools with readOnlyHint=false may mutate local desktop or application state; hosts should require approval for actions that can submit, delete, send, purchase, or overwrite data. For element-targeted actions, prefer element_index from the latest get_app_state result; click, perform_action, and set_value can also use semantic role/name/text/states selectors when the target is unique. type_text and press_key accept optional window_id, pid, app_id, wm_class, title, tty, terminal_pid, terminal_command, or terminal_cwd selectors and refuse targeted input if focus cannot be verified. After targeted keyboard input, results append focused-element feedback from AT-SPI (role, name, editable) and warn when no editable element holds focus — treat that warning as the input not landing. Screenshot, click, and input results warn when the target window or coordinate is partially or fully off-screen; use move_window/resize_window (GNOME Shell extension backend) to bring a window fully on-screen before retrying. scroll accepts the same window targeting and relative coordinates as click. get_app_state returns a compact readiness block by default; pass verbose=true for the full diagnostics dump. Electron apps expose no AT-SPI tree unless launched with --force-renderer-accessibility.
